## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `bbe4fbad5753e4e16e165a7d7d500137180a82cf`
Local-runs: probe — the head's `contractReviewRecordReading` and its regexes, copied verbatim into scratch, read the nine real records and a list of break spellings; the brief asks which real records clear, and regexes this dense are not reliably read by eye. Nothing built, no self-test, no gate re-run.
Scope: none (ungoverned; `reviewFace` returns no `hits`) + scripts/pm/check-governed-queue-guard.mjs, scripts/pm/record-recognisers.mjs, scripts/pm/check-half-states.mjs (judged as the contract files, per the brief)

PR #33736, card #33604. Read: the card body and its four comments (triage 6888140724, scope add 6890614201, claim 6891015523, os-dev-report 6891841860), the PR body and three-file list, the net diff against merge base `ee627c67` (3 files, +171 -19), and the check-runs on this head. Records measured: 6890432656 (#33686), 6890532571 (#33687), 6890622635 and 6890939010 (#33688), 6890932729, 6891274033 and 6891542450 (#33711), 6891083453 (#33720), 6891576194 (#33726).

Check-runs on the head when this was written: 52 runs; 26 success, 23 skipped, 0 failed, 3 still in progress (`Test Core (1/8)`, `Lint · PM dispatch-gates`, `Live half-state sweep`). Concluded success include `Governed Surface Queue Guard`, `Lint · scoped · tooling self-tests`, `Lint · repo & tooling gates`, `Check Changeset`, `Check PR Size`, the PR-body guards and the three type-check families. The three pending runs are the seat's to read before landing.

### ① Derived judgments

- Tier S record leg, accept set NARROWS: after the one-PASS-line rule, `recordPassVerdict` also refuses (`not-pass`, naming the comment) a record with a FAIL spelling elsewhere, an open graded finding, an unattributable grade mention, or a reading without the grade fields. Right against the ruling "the guard decides". Both legs reach it: `lowRiskRecordVerdict` ends in `recordPassVerdict`, and `runGuard` sends every other Tier S entry straight to it.
- `contractReviewVerdictLines` WIDENS what it counts: explicit lines above the heading now count (N3). Toward refusal only (a second line refuses). Its only callers in the head tree are the guard path through the reading, and self-tests. Right.
- Loader: `verdictLines` is replaced by `reading`, required; missing makes the set unavailable. Fail closed. No other reader of `recognisers.verdictLines` exists in the head tree. The open PR #33711 calls `guard.lowRiskRecordVerdict`, not the removed key, so it inherits the new reading without a break. Right.
- `record-recognisers.mjs` export surface: `contractReviewRecordReading` added beside `contractReviewVerdictLines`; nothing removed. Right.
- One reader: the new function sits beside `contractReviewVerdictLines`, reuses `CONTRACT_REVIEW_HEADING_MARKER`, `CONTRACT_REVIEW_VERDICT_EXPLICIT` and `CONTRACT_REVIEW_VERDICT_INLINE`, and the old function is now a view of it. No second parser. Right.
- Different-head records: the locator reads only records naming the current head, so a PASS that raised a finding on an older head does not block a later head that has its own record. A record CARRIED over a prose-only hop is read by the same function, so a carried record with an open graded finding now refuses; that is the consistent reading, and it is why the rule sentence in ③ matters.

### ② Semver level

`skip-changeset`, and `Check Changeset` concluded success. The diff touches `scripts/pm/**` only; nothing published. Right. Clause-②: no — agreed: no package surface, no metadata protocol.

### ③ Boundary flags

- `open_questions`: empty.
- Out-of-scope 1, the rule sentence for `contract-review.md` line 51: see S3. The PR body names #33718 as the carrier; #33718 is the card and PR #33731 is its PR. PR #33731 at head `afffd197` does not carry the sentence.
- Out-of-scope 2, records naming a graded finding need a later same-head record before re-queue: confirmed by measurement below; escalated to the seat with S1, because the measured delta records do not clear either.
- Out-of-scope 3, the H43 patrol and `check-owed-reviews.mjs` read no grades: agreed, follow-up F1 of record 6890532571, outside this card.
- Out-of-scope 4, the signed HTML comment in the PR body: the seat's convention; no effect here.

### ④ Design judgment

Measured on the real records (would the record clear the new guard, read on its own head):

- 6890432656 (#33686), 6890532571 (#33687), 6891083453 (#33720), 6891576194 (#33726): clear. Nits-only records in the two clean shapes clear, as they must.
- 6890622635 (#33688 round 1): refused, S1 and S2 open. Correct.
- 6890939010 (#33688 delta): refused, S3 open (the seat's, PR body, no head change). Correct under the ruling.
- 6890932729 (#33711 round 1): refused, S1 and S2 open, plus the count line unattributable. Correct.
- 6891274033 (#33711 delta 1): refused, S3 open. Correct in outcome.
- 6891542450 (#33711 delta 2, the clean one, the newest record on the open PR's head): REFUSED. Wrong. It closes S3, states the two clean sentences, lists nits only, and is refused because its opening line cites the prior record with its grade. See S1.

Held: the taught shapes (`S1 (should-fix) — …`, bulleted, bold, `SF1`, `S1 [..]`, `S1 — grade:`, upper case, numbered list) read open; a table row, a heading, a count line, a quoted sentence of the rule read unattributable and refuse; `No must-fix, no should-fix.`, `No must-fix. No should-fix.`, `no must-fix or should-fix`, `Nits only: no should-fix, no must-fix.` clear; `**S1: closed.**` and `S1, S2 and N1 of record N are closed on this head` clear; two explicit lines, a fenced or quoted second line, and a line above the heading refuse. The docblocks of `recordPassVerdict` and the guard header agree with the code. `quote` flattens what it echoes.

- **S1 (should-fix) — a delta record that names the grade of what it closes is refused, and the measured delta records do exactly that.** Contract: the later record that closes the findings clears; a finding mentioned as closed must not block; a nits-only record must clear. Two of the three real delta records open with `DELTA review from SHA (record N: PASS, should-fix S3, nits N7 and N8) to this head`, which the reader files as unattributable; 6891542450 is clean and is refused for that line alone. The natural closing spellings `- **S1 (should-fix): closed.**` and `S1 (should-fix) — closed on this head` are read as OPEN S1, and `No new should-fix.` / `No open should-fix.` as unattributable. The refusal then tells the seat to state `no should-fix`, which that record already does. The PR body's "grammar measured" stopped at 6890932729 and missed both #33711 deltas. Fix either side, and pin it with the measured preamble: the reader admits a citation of a prior record and a named finding whose line says closed, or `BRIEF_GRADE_LINES` and the refusal say outright that a delta record never spells the grade word of a finding it closes or cites.
- **S2 (should-fix) — N2 is not closed for every verdict-bearing form, and one negation reads the wrong way.** Ruling: a FAIL anywhere verdict-bearing never clears beside one PASS line. Beside the template PASS line these still clear: a heading-led key (`### VERDICT: FAIL`, `## Verdict: FAIL`), a table cell (`| Verdict | FAIL |`), `Overall verdict: FAIL`, `Verdict — FAIL`, and a bare `FAIL.` or `**FAIL.**` line (the separator set has no full stop). The docblock's "a line keyed `verdict:` in any case" is therefore wider than `CONTRACT_REVIEW_LINE_LEAD`, which admits no `#` and no words before the key. Separately, `CONTRACT_REVIEW_GRADE_NEGATED` takes a bare comma or `and` as carrying the negation: `No must-fix, should-fix S1 and S2 below.` reads as no grade at all, and with findings listed by id alone the record clears. That is the fail-open direction on an ambiguous line; the ruling says unreadable fails closed. Require the second `no` after a comma or `and` (keep `or` and `/`), widen the lead and the bare separator, one self-test row each.
- **S3 (should-fix, the seat's, prose face, no head change) — the card closes with its rule sentence unowned.** The card's own acceptance is "and the rule text says which". The rule needs it for the guard to be honest: line 51 ① reads "现 head 同形达档 PASS 在案", and line 52 lets the original record carry over a prose-only hop; the guard now refuses both when that record names a graded finding, including one closed on the PR body with the head unchanged. The proposed in-place sentence ("PASS 在案,无前两级") is sufficient and I would take it as written. But this PR says `Fixes #33604`, and PR #33731 (the file's owner) does not carry the sentence. Either #33731 takes the line before this lands, or the card stays open until it does. The path for a finding closed on the prose face is stated only in the refusal text and the brief line (a later full record on the same head, at tier, signed, one PASS line, closing by id alone); the rule sentence is where a seat will look.
- N1 (nit) — clean statements outside the two taught shapes refuse: `Neither must-fix nor should-fix.`, `0 must-fix, 0 should-fix`, `must-fix: none`; and `- should-fix: none` is reported as an open unnumbered finding. Fail closed, remedy is a repost; a follow-up if it bites.
- N2 (nit) — the grade is read off the hyphenated word only. `S1 (should fix)`, a non-breaking hyphen, or a finding listed by id with no grade word reads as nothing. The brief spells the word three times and all nine real records use it; accepted as the cost of closing by id alone.
- N3 (nit) — only the FIRST heading's tail is read for an inline FAIL; a second `## Contract review — FAIL` heading lower in the comment is not. No real record has two headings.
- N4 (nit) — a break-list bullet that opens `- FAIL — …` or `FAIL: …` in ④ prose refuses the record as a FAIL spelling. Fail closed; the brief could say so in a word.

No must-fix. S1, S2 and S3 each earn a delta review of their fix; S1 and S2 move the head, S3 does not.

Implemented-by: `claude/project-thread-78jrbs`
Reviewed-by: `session_01FEkQ5pjSPT7ui2EUcunaVb`

**VERDICT: PASS**

DELTA review from `bbe4fbad5753e4e16e165a7d7d500137180a82cf` (record 6891926185) to this head, PR #33736, card #33604. Read: the card body and its five comments (round-2 os-dev-report 6892238275 among them), the PR file list (three files), the net change of those three files between the two heads (one commit of the PR's own, `7c2fb525`; the rest of the range is `origin/main` merged in and is not judged), record 6891926185, and the check-runs on this head. Between the heads `check-half-states.mjs` and `check-governed-queue-guard.mjs` change; `record-recognisers.mjs` is byte-identical.

Check-runs on the head when this was written: 53 runs, all completed, NONE pending; 31 success, 22 skipped, 0 failed. Success include `Governed Surface Queue Guard`, `Lint · scoped · tooling self-tests`, `Lint · PM dispatch-gates`, `Lint · repo & tooling gates`, `Live half-state sweep`, `Test Core (1/8)`, `Test Core (2/8)`, `Check PR Size`, both PR-body guards and the four type-check families.

### ① Derived judgments

- The reader's CLEAN set WIDENS in the delta (four new shapes: a record citation, a named finding whose line says closed, a grade valued none, a qualified denial), and its FAIL-spelling set widens toward refusal. The first is the accept direction of a gate, so each new shape was tried for a record that should refuse and now clears; see ④.
- `recordPassVerdict`: only the words of the unattributable refusal change. Its order of checks and its accept set are untouched. Right.
- `CONTRACT_REVIEW_GRADE_NAMED` gains a capture group; both readers of its groups (`namedAt`, the `open` push) moved to group 3. No other reader of that regex exists in the head tree. Right.
- Every heading line is now read for an inline tail and is exempt from the keyed and bare readers; the explicit `VERDICT:` reader still runs on it. No verdict line is lost by the exemption. Right.
- One reader still: no second parser, no new export, the loader contract unchanged.

### ② Semver level

Unchanged: `skip-changeset`, `Clause-②: no`, nothing published; `scripts/pm/**` only.

### ③ Boundary flags

- `open_questions`: empty.
- The rule sentence of `contract-review.md` line 51 is carried by PR #33731, which is open and unmerged at `51787fa6`; its record 6891987837 judged the sentence. This head's tree does not hold it. Order of landing is the seat's; record 6891987837 found no contradiction either way.
- The dev did not patch the PR body (os-dev.md: the seat writes later bodies); the round-2 body is a project file. The seat's.
- N2 and N4 of record 6891926185 are left as accepted by the dev; agreed.

### ④ Design judgment

Prior findings, by id:

- **S1: closed.** Re-measured on the real records, each read on its own head. CLEAR: 6890432656 (#33686), 6890532571 (#33687), 6891083453 (#33720), 6891576194 (#33726), 6891542450 (#33711 final delta), 6891987837 (#33731 delta). REFUSED: 6890622635 (#33688 round 1, S1 and S2 open), 6890939010 (#33688 delta, S3 open on the PR body), 6890932729 (#33711 round 1, S1 and S2 open plus the count line), 6891274033 (#33711 delta 1, S3 open plus the count line), 6891667603 (#33731 round 1, its S1 spelled with a comma and so unattributable, plus the basis line), 6892058186 (#33732 delta, D1 open), 6891926185 (this PR's round 1, three open). Every one is right: the six that clear name nothing open in the upper two grades, and each of the seven refused names one. Both clean delta records now clear, including the one that was wrongly refused. The refusal text names the shapes the reader takes and no longer asks for a sentence the record carries. Pinned on the measured preamble, with a control that a new named finding beside a citation still refuses.
- **S2: closed.** Beside one PASS line each of these refuses as a FAIL spelling: `### VERDICT: FAIL`, `## Verdict: FAIL`, `| Verdict | FAIL |`, `Overall verdict: FAIL`, `Verdict — FAIL`, a bare `FAIL.`, `**FAIL.**`, and a second `## Contract review — FAIL` heading. After a comma or `and` the second grade needs its own `no`: `No must-fix, should-fix S1 and S2 below.`, `No open must-fix, should-fix S2 below`, `No open must-fix and should-fix S2 below`, `No open must-fix; should-fix S2 below`, `0 must-fix, 1 should-fix` are each unattributable and refused; `No must-fix and no should-fix.` and `No must-fix, nor should-fix` clear. One pin row each in both self-tests.
- N1 taken: `Neither must-fix nor should-fix.`, `0 must-fix, 0 should-fix`, `must-fix: none`, `- should-fix: none` clear. N3 taken: every heading's tail is read, a quoted one included.
- S3 of record 6891926185 was the seat's and moves no head; see ③.

New at this head:

- **S1 (should-fix) — the closed-or-none reading takes the first WORD after the grade, so a finding named in the taught shape clears whenever its title opens with that word.** `CONTRACT_REVIEW_GRADE_NAMED_STATE` ends at `(closed|none)\b` and reads nothing after it. Measured on this head, each beside the template PASS line, each CLEARS: `S1 (should-fix): closed in part, still open for X`; `- **S1 (should-fix) — closed in part; the table cell still clears.**`; `**S2 (should-fix) — Closed PRs are still read as merged by the audit.**`; `- **S2 (should-fix) — none of the three ablations ran on the committed head.**`; `S1 (should-fix) — closed on the prior head, reopened by this delta`; `- should-fix: none of S1, S2 is fixed`. At `bbe4fbad` every one of these read OPEN and refused, so the delta turned a refusal into a clearance, on the exact shape the brief teaches for an open finding. It is the card's own defect (a PASS that lists an open finding of the upper grades clears) for the subset of titles that start with one of two ordinary words; findings about closed PRs and "none of the callers" titles are ordinary in this fleet. Fix in the one regex: after the state word admit only the end of the line, closing emphasis, a full stop or semicolon, or the measured tail (`on this head`, `at this head`, `here`); anything else leaves the finding open. Pin `closed in part`, `none of …` and a title opening `Closed …` as refusals beside the existing clean row. No effect on the thirteen measured records: none uses a closed line with a grade word.
- N1 (nit) — the citation excuses everything inside its brackets, and the qualified denial denies only additions. `S1 stays open (record 6891926185: should-fix, not fixed on this head).` and `No new should-fix. S1 of record 6891926185 stays open.` clear. Both rest on a finding kept open by id alone with no taught line, which is the cost record 6891926185 accepted as its N2; the delta only stops such a line from tripping the unattributable net. The pinned control covers the realistic case (a named finding beside a citation).
- N2 (nit) — verdict-bearing spellings still outside the reader, all exotic beside a template PASS line: `Verdict: FAILED`, `Verdict is FAIL`, `Verdict (delta): FAIL`, a table whose verdict column is a header row (`| Tier | Verdict |` over `| … | FAIL |`), `| FAIL | Verdict |`, a mark before the cell's word, `FAIL!`, and a heading tail reading `— PASS withdrawn, FAIL` (the inline reader stops at the first word). None is in any measured record.
- N3 (nit) — refusals of clean text, toward closed: a prose line led by up to two words and the key, such as `- Leg verdict: fail-closed reading holds.`, is now a FAIL spelling (the two-word allowance widened it); `S1 (should-fix) is closed` reads open; a `### Should-fix` section heading over `None.` reads as an open unnumbered finding. Remedy is a repost.
- N4 (nit) — `BRIEF_GRADE_LINES` still teaches only closing by id alone. The reader is now wider than the brief, which is the safe side; no change owed.

Did the delta break anything else: no. The eight taught open shapes (bulleted, bold, numbered, quoted, `SF1`, square bracket, upper case, heading-led) still read open; a table row and a count line still refuse; prose that mentions the word FAIL after a comma is still not a spelling.

No must-fix. S1 of this record earns a delta review of its fix and moves the head.

### ① Derived judgments

- The reader's CLEAN set NARROWS in the delta: the closed-or-none state now clears a named finding only when the state word ends it. Every line the old regex opened on and the new one refuses moves toward refusal. The one accept-direction piece is the allowance for a full stop that closes a bold title followed by a new sentence; it is a subset of what the prior head cleared, so nothing clears now that refused at `7c2fb525`. Tried for fail-open in ④.
- The FAIL-spelling set WIDENS toward refusal only: a parenthetical after the key, `is` as the separator, FAILED and FAILS, a table row read cell by cell in either order, `!` after a bare word, any caps word in a heading's tail. No spelling that refused at the prior head clears now (the fourteen forms of rounds 1 and 2 re-run, all refuse).
- `CONTRACT_REVIEW_FAIL_CELL` changed from a regex to an object with a `test` method; its one caller calls `.test(line)` and no other reader of the name exists in the head tree. Right.
- `recordPassVerdict`, the loader and the export surface are untouched by the delta. One reader still, no second parser.

- The dev patched the PR body this round on the seat's instruction and names the conflict with os-dev.md rule 3 in its report. The seat's.
- The body's self-test counts (526 / 5268 / 389) are the dev's local runs; the CI job that runs the three self-tests concluded success on this head. Not re-run here.

### ④ Design judgment

Prior findings, by id:

- **S1 of record 6892305129: closed.** `CONTRACT_REVIEW_GRADE_NAMED_STATE` now requires, after the state word, an optional measured tail (`on this head`, `at this head`, `here`) and then either the end of the line past closing emphasis with at most one full stop or semicolon, or a full stop directly closing a double-mark bold title and a new sentence. Measured, each beside the template PASS line: the six lines of that record's finding all read open and refuse again (`closed in part, still open for X`; `closed in part; the table cell still clears.`; a title opening `Closed PRs`; `none of the three ablations ran`; `closed on the prior head, reopened by this delta`; `none of S1, S2 is fixed` under a bare grade key). Also refused: `closed. Still open for X` with no bold, `closed here; still open for X`, `closed on this head except Y` with and without a comma, `closed here, not there`, `closed, reopened`, `closed-then-reopened`, `closed/open`, `closed?`, `closed!`, `not closed`, `closed heretofore`, nested emphasis around the word inside a longer title, a full stop placed outside the bold, a single-star title, a table row. `closed; S2 (GRADE) below stays open` refuses twice over (S1 reads open, the second grade word is unattributable). A closed bold title whose body restates the grade word, on the same line or the next, refuses as unattributable. Clean controls clear: `closed.`, `closed;`, `closed here.`, `closed on this head.`, `Closed.`, a grade carrying a note inside its bracket, a quoted line, the square-bracket form, a closed bold title followed by a plain sentence. Pinned in both self-tests, with the ablation named in the PR body.
- N2 of record 6892305129, the cheap spellings: taken, and each refuses beside one PASS line as a FAIL spelling. Measured: the key valued FAILED, the key with `is`, the key with a parenthetical, the reversed table row, the bare word with `!`, and a late caps word in a heading tail. One pin row in each self-test.
- S1 and S2 of record 6891926185 stay closed: the measured delta preamble still cites, a new named finding beside a citation still refuses, the comma and `and` denials still need their own `no`, the eight FAIL forms of that round still refuse. S3 of that record was the seat's; its sentence is on this head through main (see ③).

The real-record measurement, each record read on its own head:

- CLEAR (8): 6890432656 (#33686), 6890532571 (#33687), 6891083453 (#33720), 6891576194 (#33726), 6891542450 (#33711 final delta), 6891987837 (#33731 delta), 6892490875 (the follow-up to #33711's nits), 6892612604 (#33732 final delta). Each was read line by line for a finding of the upper two grades: none names one. All are nits-only or close by id, and all clear, as they must.
- REFUSED (9): 6890622635 (S1, S2 open), 6890939010 (S3 open), 6890932729 (S1, S2 open and a count line), 6891274033 (S3 open and two unattributable lines), 6891667603 (its S1 spelled with a comma, unattributable, with the basis line), 6892058186 (D1 open), 6892622399 (its two open findings S1 and S2, spelled with a comma, unattributable, with the closing sentence), 6891926185 (S1, S2, S3 open), 6892305129 (S1 open).
